It was sponsored by [[Emirates (airline)|Emirates]] and known as the '''Emirates FA Cup''' for sponsorship reasons. The FA Cup is the main domestic cup competition for men's football teams in England. The qualifying competition began on 3 August 2024, with the tournament proper starting on 2 November 2024. The [[2025 FA Cup final|final]] was played at [[Wembley Stadium]], [[London]], on 17 May 2025. [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] won the tournament for the first time, defeating [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] in the final and winning their first ever major trophy. As the winners, Crystal Palace earned the right to play against the [[2024–25 Premier League]] champions, [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], in the [[2025 FA Community Shield]], as well as qualifying for the [[2025–26 UEFA Conference League]] play-off round.{{Cite web |last=Johnson |first=Dale |date=2025-07-11 |title=Crystal Palace out of Europa League amid Lyon conflict |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/45715071/crystal-palace-demoted-conference-league-amid-ownership-conflict |access-date=2025-08-15 |website=ESPN}}{{Cite news |last=Aarons |first=Ed |date=2025-07-09 |title=Crystal Palace's Europa League hopes dealt blow after Lyon win relegation appeal |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/jul/09/crystal-palace-europa-league-hopes-dealt-blow-after-lyon-win-relegation-appeal |access-date=2025-08-15 |work=The Guardian |issn=0261-3077}}{{cite web |title=The CFCB First Chamber renders decision on Crystal Palace and Olympique Lyonnais |url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/029b-1e361573fefc-94aa466245fc-1000--the-cfcb-first-chamber-renders-decision-on-crystal-palace-an/ |website=[[UEFA]] |access-date=11 July 2025}}{{Cite web |date=2025-08-11 |title=Crystal Palace lose appeal against demotion from Europa League to Conference League |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c1kzzpp04kgo |access-date=2025-08-15 |website=BBC Sport }} For City, this was their third consecutive FA Cup final appearance, and second consecutive defeat. Defending champions [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]], having beaten [[Manchester derby|rivals]] Manchester City in the [[2024 FA Cup final|2024 final]] to win their 13th title, were eliminated by [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] in the fifth round. ==Teams== The FA Cup is a [[Single-elimination tournament|knockout]] competition with 124 teams taking part from the first round proper, and all trying to reach the final at Wembley Stadium on 17 May 2025. The competition consists of the 92 teams from the Football League system (20 teams from the [[Premier League]] and the 72 in total from the [[EFL Championship]], [[EFL League One]] and [[EFL League Two]]) plus the 32 surviving teams out of 653 teams from the [[National League System]] that started the competition in the [[2024–25 FA Cup qualifying rounds|qualifying rounds]]. The total 745 entrants was an increase of 13 from the previous season, and the most since 758 entrants were accepted in [[2012–13 FA Cup|2012–13]]. [[Video assistant referee|VAR]] will be used in all matches from the fifth round onwards (and none prior), whereas in previous seasons it was used for all matches held in [[Premier League]] grounds and at [[Wembley Stadium]].{{cite news |date=16 December 2024 |title=VAR confirmed for Emirates FA Cup from fifth round onwards |url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2024/dec/16/var-to-be-used-in-emirates-fa-cup-fifth-round-onwards-20241612 |publisher=The Football Association |access-date=8 January 2025}} ==Qualifying== {{for|all qualifying round results|2024–25 FA Cup qualifying rounds}} Teams that are not members of either the [[Premier League]] or [[English Football League]] competed in the qualifying rounds to secure one of 32 available places in the first round. The six-round qualifying competition began with the extra preliminary round on 3 August 2024, with the fourth and final qualifying round kicking off on 12 October. The winners from the fourth qualifying round were [[Rushall Olympic F.C.|Rushall Olympic]], [[Tamworth F.C.|Tamworth]], [[Oldham Athletic A.F.C.|Oldham Athletic]], [[Brackley Town F.C.|Brackley Town]], [[Kettering Town F.C.|Kettering Town]], [[Solihull Moors F.C.|Solihull Moors]], [[Rochdale A.F.C.|Rochdale]], [[Scarborough Athletic F.C.|Scarborough Athletic]], [[York City F.C.|York City]], [[Harborough Town F.C.|Harborough Town]], [[Curzon Ashton F.C.|Curzon Ashton]], [[Gainsborough Trinity F.C.|Gainsborough Trinity]], [[Hednesford Town F.C.|Hednesford Town]], [[Alfreton Town F.C.|Alfreton Town]], [[Guiseley A.F.C.|Guiseley]], [[Maidenhead United F.C.|Maidenhead United]], [[Horsham F.C.|Horsham]], [[Aldershot Town F.C.|Aldershot Town]], [[Southend United F.C.|Southend United]], [[Boreham Wood F.C.|Boreham Wood]], [[Weston-super-Mare A.F.C.|Weston-super-Mare]], [[Sutton United F.C.|Sutton United]], [[Dagenham & Redbridge F.C.|Dagenham & Redbridge]], [[Wealdstone F.C.|Wealdstone]], [[Barnet F.C.|Barnet]], [[Chesham United F.C.|Chesham United]], [[Tonbridge Angels F.C.|Tonbridge Angels]], [[Woking F.C.|Woking]], [[Forest Green Rovers F.C.|Forest Green Rovers]], [[Maidstone United F.C.|Maidstone United]], [[Worthing F.C.|Worthing]] and [[Braintree Town F.C.|Braintree Town]]. Rushall Olympic and Harborough Town were appearing in the competition proper for the first time. Of the others, Braintree Town had last featured at this stage in [[2016–17 FA Cup|2016–17]], Wealdstone had last done so in [[2015–16 FA Cup|2015–16]], Tamworth and Hednesford Town had last done so in [[2013–14 FA Cup|2013–14]] and Kettering Town had last done so in [[2011–12 FA Cup|2011–12]]. ==First round== A total of 80 teams played in the first round: 32 winners from the fourth qualifying round, 24 from [[EFL League Two|League Two]] (tier 4), and 24 from [[EFL League One|League One]] (tier 3).
